title: Data Science Project Showcase: Analyzing a Real-World Dataset
description: Students will conduct a complete data science workflow on a provided dataset and present their findings through a 10-minute presentation. This assessment evaluates students' ability to perform exploratory data analysis, create meaningful visualizations, draw insights, and communicate findings effectively to a non-technical audience.
learning_objectives: Perform exploratory data analysis using appropriate statistical methods and visualizations
Identify patterns, trends, and outliers in datasets using descriptive statistics
Create clear and appropriate data visualizations using tools like Python/R or Excel
Communicate data insights effectively to non-technical stakeholders
Apply the data science workflow from data exploration to actionable recommendations
criteria: Data Exploration and Analysis (25 points): Demonstrates thorough exploration of the dataset including summary statistics, data quality assessment, identification of missing values, and appropriate statistical analysis techniques

Visualization Quality (25 points): Creates 3-4 clear, appropriate, and well-labeled visualizations that effectively communicate key findings. Charts are properly formatted with titles, axis labels, and legends where needed

Insights and Interpretation (25 points): Identifies meaningful patterns, trends, or relationships in the data and provides accurate interpretations. Makes at least 2 specific, data-driven recommendations based on findings

Presentation and Communication (25 points): Delivers a clear, organized 8-10 minute presentation using non-technical language. Maintains good eye contact, speaks clearly, and effectively explains visualizations to the audience

title: Ethical AI and Algorithmic Bias: Case Study Analysis and Mitigation Strategy Discussion
description: Students will analyze real-world cases of algorithmic bias, evaluate their societal impact, and propose comprehensive mitigation strategies while engaging in peer discussion about the ethical implications of data science practices in high-stakes applications.
learning_objectives: Critically evaluate ethical implications and potential biases in machine learning algorithms and data science applications
Analyze the intersection of technical implementation choices and societal outcomes in data-driven systems
Synthesize technical knowledge with ethical frameworks to propose actionable solutions for bias mitigation
Communicate complex technical and ethical concepts effectively to diverse stakeholders
criteria: Case Analysis and Technical Understanding (25 points): Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of the technical causes of bias in the chosen case, accurately identifies specific algorithmic, data collection, or preprocessing issues, and explains the mechanism by which bias manifested in the system's outputs

Ethical Framework Application and Impact Assessment (25 points): Applies relevant ethical frameworks (fairness, accountability, transparency, etc.) to evaluate societal impact, considers multiple stakeholder perspectives, and demonstrates understanding of both immediate and long-term consequences

Mitigation Strategy Development (25 points): Proposes specific, technically feasible solutions addressing root causes, considers implementation challenges and trade-offs, includes both technical interventions and process improvements, and addresses monitoring and evaluation mechanisms

Discussion Engagement and Professional Communication (25 points): Provides substantive responses to at least 3 peers with constructive feedback or alternative perspectives, uses appropriate technical terminology while remaining accessible, demonstrates respectful engagement with differing viewpoints, and contributes meaningfully to collective understanding

title: Advanced Mathematical Research Presentation: Novel Applications of Differential Equations
description: Students will conduct independent research on cutting-edge applications of differential equations in modern science or engineering, then present their findings in a 20-minute academic presentation that demonstrates mastery of advanced mathematical concepts, research methodology, and communication skills.
learning_objectives: Apply advanced differential equation theory to solve complex real-world problems
Synthesize mathematical research from primary academic sources
Demonstrate mastery of mathematical proof techniques and rigorous argumentation
Communicate sophisticated mathematical concepts clearly to expert audiences
Evaluate the significance and limitations of mathematical models in practical applications
criteria: Mathematical Rigor and Accuracy (25 points): Demonstrates flawless understanding of differential equation theory, presents mathematically sound derivations and proofs, uses precise mathematical notation and terminology, shows mastery of relevant theorems and techniques

Research Quality and Innovation (25 points): Selects cutting-edge, significant application area; synthesizes multiple high-quality academic sources; demonstrates original thinking in analysis or approach; identifies gaps in current research or proposes novel extensions

Presentation Delivery and Clarity (25 points): Delivers clear, well-organized presentation with logical flow; uses appropriate visual aids and mathematical notation; maintains audience engagement; demonstrates confidence with material; manages time effectively within 20-minute limit

Critical Analysis and Problem-Solving (25 points): Provides thorough analysis of mathematical model limitations; discusses assumptions and their validity; compares multiple solution approaches; addresses potential extensions or generalizations; demonstrates deep conceptual understanding

title: Advanced Calculus Problem-Solving Assessment: Optimization and Related Rates
description: Students will demonstrate mastery of advanced calculus concepts by solving complex optimization problems and related rates scenarios. This assessment evaluates analytical thinking, mathematical modeling, and the application of derivatives to real-world situations.
learning_objectives: Apply optimization techniques to solve complex multi-variable problems with constraints
Model and solve related rates problems involving multiple changing quantities
Demonstrate proficiency in setting up and solving differential equations from word problems
Communicate mathematical reasoning clearly through detailed solution processes
criteria: Problem Setup and Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Correctly identifies variables, establishes relationships, sets up equations, and defines constraints from problem descriptions
Mathematical Procedures and Calculations (25 points): Accurately applies calculus techniques including differentiation rules, chain rule, implicit differentiation, and algebraic manipulations
Solution Accuracy and Verification (25 points): Arrives at correct final answers, checks solutions for reasonableness, identifies maximum/minimum values correctly, and verifies units
Mathematical Communication and Reasoning (25 points): Shows clear step-by-step work, explains reasoning behind each step, uses proper mathematical notation, and presents solutions in logical sequence

title: Distributed Web Crawler with Microservices Architecture
description: Students will design and implement a scalable distributed web crawler system using microservices architecture, incorporating containerization, message queues, data persistence, and monitoring. The system must handle concurrent crawling, avoid duplicate URLs, respect robots.txt, and provide real-time analytics through a web dashboard.
learning_objectives: Design and implement distributed systems using microservices architecture patterns
Apply advanced concurrency and parallel processing techniques in a real-world application
Integrate multiple technologies including containerization, message queues, and databases
Implement comprehensive testing strategies for distributed systems
Demonstrate understanding of system scalability, fault tolerance, and performance optimization
criteria: System Architecture & Design (25 points): Clear microservices separation, proper API design, scalable architecture documentation, appropriate technology choices, comprehensive system diagram with data flow

Implementation Quality (25 points): Clean, maintainable code following best practices, proper error handling, efficient algorithms, appropriate use of design patterns, comprehensive logging and monitoring

Technical Features (25 points): Functional distributed crawling, duplicate URL prevention, robots.txt compliance, data persistence with proper schema design, real-time dashboard with meaningful metrics

Testing & Documentation (25 points): Unit tests with >80% coverage, integration tests for microservices communication, load testing results, complete README with setup instructions, API documentation, architectural decisions document

title: Mathematical Problem-Solving Strategies Discussion: Real-World Applications
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion analyzing different mathematical problem-solving approaches by examining real-world scenarios involving systems of linear equations, quadratic functions, and statistical analysis. Students must demonstrate understanding of multiple solution methods, justify their chosen approaches, and critically evaluate peers' strategies.
learning_objectives: Apply multiple problem-solving strategies to solve systems of linear equations and quadratic functions
Analyze and interpret mathematical solutions in real-world contexts
Communicate mathematical reasoning clearly using appropriate terminology and notation
Evaluate and critique mathematical approaches used by others
criteria: Initial Problem Analysis (25 points): Correctly identifies mathematical concepts in scenarios, selects appropriate solution methods, shows complete work with proper notation, and arrives at accurate solutions

Real-World Application & Interpretation (25 points): Clearly explains what solutions mean in practical context, discusses limitations or assumptions, and connects mathematical results to real-world implications
Mathematical Communication (25 points): Uses precise mathematical language and notation, explanations are clear and logical, work is well-organized, and reasoning is easy to follow

Peer Engagement & Critical Thinking (25 points): Provides substantive responses to at least two peers, offers alternative approaches or identifies errors, asks thoughtful questions, and demonstrates understanding of others' methods

title: Advanced Algorithm Design and Analysis: Technical Presentation
description: Students will design, analyze, and present a novel algorithmic solution to a complex computational problem, demonstrating mastery of algorithm design paradigms, complexity analysis, and technical communication skills.
learning_objectives: Design efficient algorithms using advanced paradigms (dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, divide-and-conquer, graph algorithms)
Perform rigorous time and space complexity analysis using asymptotic notation
Evaluate trade-offs between different algorithmic approaches and justify design decisions
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
Implement and validate algorithmic solutions with appropriate testing strategies
criteria: Algorithm Design and Innovation (25 points): Demonstrates creativity and technical soundness in problem selection and solution approach. Shows clear understanding of chosen algorithm paradigm(s). Solution must be non-trivial and go beyond textbook examples.

Theoretical Analysis (25 points): Provides rigorous mathematical analysis of time/space complexity. Includes best-case, average-case, and worst-case scenarios where applicable. Compares with alternative approaches and justifies optimality claims.

Implementation and Validation (25 points): Code is well-structured, documented, and demonstrates the algorithm working on test cases. Includes edge cases and performance benchmarks. Shows proper software engineering practices.

Presentation Quality and Technical Communication (25 points): Clear explanation of problem motivation, solution approach, and results. Effective use of visual aids. Handles questions confidently. Presentation flows logically and stays within time limits.

title: Data Collection and Statistical Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will design and conduct a simple statistical survey, collect real data, analyze their findings using basic statistical measures, and present their results in a structured lab report format.
learning_objectives: Apply basic statistical concepts (mean, median, mode, range) to real-world data
Create and interpret simple data visualizations (bar graphs, histograms)
Demonstrate understanding of data collection methods and potential sources of bias
Communicate mathematical findings clearly using appropriate terminology
criteria: Data Collection & Methodology (25 points): Survey question is clear and appropriate, sample size meets minimum requirements (20+ responses), data collection method is described, potential sources of bias are identified

Mathematical Calculations (25 points): All statistical measures (mean, median, mode, range) are calculated correctly with work shown, calculations are clearly labeled and organized, appropriate units are used throughout

Data Visualization (25 points): Graph type is appropriate for data collected, graph includes proper title, axis labels, and scale, data is accurately represented visually, graph is neat and professional in appearance

Analysis & Communication (25 points): Results are interpreted correctly in context, conclusions are supported by data, mathematical vocabulary is used appropriately, report follows required format and is well-organized

title: Programming Languages Discussion: Comparing Python and Java for Beginners
description: Students will engage in a structured online discussion comparing Python and Java programming languages, focusing on syntax, ease of learning, and practical applications. Students must make an initial post and respond meaningfully to two peers' posts.
learning_objectives: Compare and contrast fundamental characteristics of different programming languages
Analyze the appropriateness of programming languages for specific tasks and beginner learning
Demonstrate understanding of basic programming concepts through written communication
Engage constructively in technical discussions with peers
criteria: Initial Post Quality (35 points): Demonstrates clear understanding of both languages, includes specific examples of syntax differences, discusses at least 2 practical applications, uses proper technical terminology, meets 250-300 word requirement

Peer Response Quality (25 points): Provides 2 substantive responses (100+ words each) that extend the conversation, asks thoughtful questions or offers additional insights, demonstrates engagement with peers' ideas rather than simple agreement

Technical Accuracy (25 points): Information about both languages is factually correct, code examples (if included) are syntactically accurate, demonstrates understanding of basic programming concepts like variables, loops, or functions

Communication and Professionalism (15 points): Uses clear, professional writing with proper grammar and spelling, organizes ideas logically, responds respectfully to peers, posts within specified timeframe

title: Real-World Data Science Project: From Raw Data to Business Insights
description: Students will conduct a complete data science project using a provided messy dataset, performing data cleaning, exploratory analysis, modeling, and presenting actionable business recommendations through a 12-15 minute presentation with supporting materials.
learning_objectives: Apply end-to-end data science workflow including data cleaning, exploration, and modeling
Communicate technical findings effectively to non-technical stakeholders
Make data-driven business recommendations based on analytical results
Demonstrate proficiency with data visualization and statistical analysis tools
criteria: Data Preparation & Methodology (25 points): Quality of data cleaning process, handling of missing values, feature engineering decisions, and appropriateness of analytical methods chosen
Analysis & Modeling (25 points): Depth of exploratory data analysis, validity of statistical tests/models used, interpretation of results, and acknowledgment of limitations
Visualization & Communication (25 points): Clarity and effectiveness of charts/graphs, logical flow of presentation, appropriate use of technical vs. non-technical language for audience
Business Impact & Recommendations (25 points): Relevance and feasibility of recommendations, clear connection between data insights and business value, consideration of implementation challenges

title: Distributed Systems Consensus Algorithm Implementation and Performance Analysis
description: Students will implement the Raft consensus algorithm, deploy it across multiple nodes, and conduct comprehensive performance analysis under various failure scenarios. This assessment evaluates advanced distributed systems concepts, algorithm implementation skills, and empirical research methodology.
learning_objectives: Design and implement fault-tolerant distributed algorithms with proper handling of network partitions and node failures
Analyze and evaluate distributed system performance under varying load conditions and failure scenarios
Apply empirical research methods to validate theoretical concepts in distributed computing
Demonstrate proficiency in concurrent programming and inter-process communication protocols
criteria: Implementation Quality (25 points): Correct Raft algorithm implementation including leader election, log replication, and safety properties. Code must handle edge cases, demonstrate proper concurrency control, and include comprehensive error handling.

Experimental Design and Execution (25 points): Well-designed experiments testing performance under different scenarios (varying cluster sizes, network delays, failure rates). Proper use of metrics, statistical significance testing, and reproducible methodology.

Analysis and Insights (25 points): Thorough analysis of results with clear explanations of performance characteristics, identification of bottlenecks, comparison with theoretical expectations, and discussion of trade-offs between consistency and availability.

Technical Communication (25 points): Clear, well-structured lab report with proper use of technical terminology, effective visualizations, complete documentation of setup procedures, and professional presentation of findings.

title: Data Science Fundamentals Quiz: Exploring Data Types and Basic Analysis
description: A comprehensive quiz assessing students' understanding of fundamental data science concepts including data types, basic statistical measures, data visualization principles, and introductory data cleaning techniques. Students will demonstrate knowledge through multiple choice questions, short calculations, and scenario-based problem solving.
learning_objectives: Identify and classify different types of data (nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio)
Calculate basic descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, standard deviation)
Recognize appropriate data visualization methods for different data types
Understand fundamental data quality issues and basic cleaning approaches
criteria: Data Types and Classification (25 points): Correctly identifies qualitative vs quantitative data, distinguishes between discrete and continuous variables, and classifies data using appropriate measurement scales

Descriptive Statistics (25 points): Accurately calculates measures of central tendency and variability, interprets statistical results in context, and identifies when different measures are most appropriate

Data Visualization Principles (25 points): Selects appropriate chart types for different data scenarios, identifies misleading visualizations, and understands basic design principles for effective data presentation

Data Quality and Cleaning (25 points): Recognizes common data quality issues (missing values, outliers, inconsistencies), understands impact of data problems on analysis, and knows basic cleaning strategies

title: Community Data Analysis Project: Statistical Investigation and Presentation
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive statistical investigation of a real-world community issue using data collection, analysis, and mathematical modeling. They will present their findings through both written report and visual presentation, demonstrating understanding of statistical concepts and their practical applications.
learning_objectives: Apply statistical measures of central tendency and variability to real-world data sets
Create and interpret various types of graphs and charts for data visualization
Use mathematical modeling to make predictions and draw conclusions from data
Communicate mathematical findings clearly using appropriate terminology and notation
Evaluate the reliability and validity of data sources and statistical claims
criteria: Data Collection and Organization (25 points): Gathers appropriate, reliable data from multiple sources; organizes data systematically in tables/spreadsheets; clearly documents sources and methodology; demonstrates understanding of sample size and bias considerations

Mathematical Analysis (25 points): Correctly calculates measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and variability (range, standard deviation); creates appropriate graphs/charts with proper labels and scales; applies relevant mathematical concepts accurately with clear work shown

Interpretation and Conclusions (25 points): Makes logical connections between data and real-world context; draws reasonable conclusions supported by mathematical evidence; identifies patterns and trends; discusses limitations and potential sources of error; makes data-driven predictions or recommendations

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Written report is well-organized with clear mathematical explanations; uses proper mathematical vocabulary and notation; visual presentation effectively communicates findings; includes appropriate graphs, charts, and mathematical representations; demonstrates understanding through clear explanations

title: Ethics and Bias in Machine Learning: A Critical Analysis Discussion
description: Students will engage in a structured discussion analyzing real-world cases of algorithmic bias, evaluate ethical frameworks for ML deployment, and propose comprehensive solutions for bias mitigation in data science projects.
learning_objectives: Critically evaluate ethical implications and potential biases in machine learning models and data science workflows
Apply established ethical frameworks to assess real-world AI/ML deployment scenarios
Synthesize technical and ethical considerations to propose actionable bias mitigation strategies
Communicate complex ethical and technical concepts effectively to diverse stakeholders
criteria: Initial Analysis Post (25 points): Demonstrates deep understanding of algorithmic bias concepts, provides thorough analysis of assigned case study with specific technical details, correctly applies ethical frameworks, and presents well-reasoned conclusions supported by credible sources

Peer Responses and Engagement (25 points): Provides substantive, thoughtful responses to at least 3 peers, asks probing questions that advance discussion, respectfully challenges assumptions with evidence, and builds upon others' ideas constructively

Technical Depth and Accuracy (25 points): Accurately explains technical concepts related to bias sources (data, algorithmic, evaluation), demonstrates understanding of detection methods and metrics, and shows knowledge of current industry practices and tools

Solution Synthesis and Innovation (25 points): Proposes comprehensive, implementable solutions that address both technical and organizational aspects, considers stakeholder perspectives and real-world constraints, and demonstrates creative thinking while maintaining technical feasibility

title: My Favorite Number: A Mathematical Story Presentation
description: Students will create and deliver a 5-7 minute presentation about their favorite number (1-100), exploring its mathematical properties, real-world applications, and personal significance while demonstrating basic mathematical concepts through visual aids and clear explanations.
learning_objectives: Identify and explain basic mathematical properties (odd/even, factors, multiples)
Connect mathematical concepts to real-world applications and personal experiences
Communicate mathematical ideas clearly using appropriate vocabulary and visual representations
Demonstrate understanding of number relationships and patterns
criteria: Mathematical Content (25 points): Correctly identifies at least 4 mathematical properties of chosen number (odd/even, factors, prime/composite, place value, multiples). Shows accurate calculations and uses proper mathematical vocabulary.

Real-World Connections (25 points): Provides 2-3 meaningful examples of how the number appears in everyday life, nature, or specific contexts. Explains why these connections are significant and interesting.
Presentation Skills (25 points): Speaks clearly and confidently, maintains eye contact, stays within time limit (5-7 minutes), engages audience appropriately. Shows enthusiasm for the topic.

Visual Aids and Organization (25 points): Uses at least 2 visual elements (poster, drawings, objects, etc.) effectively. Presentation follows logical sequence: introduction, mathematical properties, real-world examples, conclusion.

title: Predictive Analytics Pipeline: Customer Churn Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will conduct a comprehensive end-to-end data science project analyzing customer churn data. This assessment evaluates their ability to perform exploratory data analysis, implement multiple machine learning algorithms, validate model performance, and communicate findings through a professional lab report with code documentation.
learning_objectives: Apply advanced statistical analysis and visualization techniques to extract meaningful insights from complex datasets
Design and implement multiple machine learning algorithms including feature engineering and hyperparameter optimization
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and validation techniques for business classification problems
Communicate technical findings effectively through professional documentation and data-driven recommendations
criteria: Data Exploration & Preprocessing (25 points): Comprehensive EDA with 8+ meaningful visualizations, proper handling of missing values, outlier detection, feature scaling, and clear documentation of data quality issues and preprocessing decisions

Model Implementation & Engineering (25 points): Implementation of minimum 3 algorithms (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting), proper feature engineering including categorical encoding and feature selection, hyperparameter tuning using cross-validation, and clean, well-commented code

Model Evaluation & Validation (25 points): Use of appropriate metrics (precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC), k-fold cross-validation implementation, confusion matrix analysis, feature importance analysis, and statistical significance testing of model comparisons

Professional Communication & Business Impact (25 points): Executive summary with clear business recommendations, technical methodology section, results interpretation with visualizations, discussion of limitations, and professional formatting with proper citations

title: Advanced Calculus and Real Analysis Comprehensive Quiz
description: A comprehensive assessment evaluating students' mastery of advanced calculus concepts including multivariable optimization, series convergence, complex integration, and rigorous proof techniques. Students will solve challenging problems requiring deep theoretical understanding and computational proficiency.
learning_objectives: Apply advanced optimization techniques to solve multivariable calculus problems with constraints
Analyze convergence and divergence of infinite series using multiple convergence tests
Evaluate complex line integrals and apply residue theorem for contour integration
Construct rigorous mathematical proofs using epsilon-delta definitions and logical reasoning
criteria: Problem Setup and Mathematical Modeling (25 points): Correctly identifies problem type, sets up appropriate equations/functions, clearly defines variables and constraints, demonstrates understanding of underlying mathematical concepts

Solution Method and Computational Accuracy (25 points): Selects appropriate solution techniques, executes calculations correctly, shows all intermediate steps, arrives at correct numerical or algebraic answers

Mathematical Reasoning and Proof Structure (25 points): Constructs logically sound arguments, uses proper mathematical notation and terminology, provides clear justification for each step, demonstrates rigorous thinking

Communication and Presentation (25 points): Presents solutions clearly and organized manner, explains reasoning effectively, uses appropriate mathematical language, provides complete and well-formatted responses

title: Personal Budget Calculator - Console Application Project
description: Students will design and implement a console-based personal budget calculator that allows users to input income and expenses, categorize transactions, and generate basic financial reports. This project assesses fundamental programming concepts including variables, data structures, control flow, functions, and file I/O.
learning_objectives: Apply fundamental programming constructs (variables, loops, conditionals) to solve real-world problems
Implement and utilize appropriate data structures (lists, dictionaries) for data organization
Design and implement modular functions with proper parameter passing and return values
Demonstrate basic file input/output operations for data persistence
Practice debugging and testing strategies for program validation
criteria: Program Functionality (25 points): Application successfully performs all required operations (add income/expenses, categorization, balance calculation, basic reporting) with proper error handling for invalid inputs
Code Structure and Organization (25 points): Code is well-organized with meaningful function decomposition, appropriate variable names, consistent formatting, and clear separation of concerns

Data Management (25 points): Proper implementation of data structures for storing transactions, effective use of file I/O for saving/loading data, and appropriate data validation throughout the program

Documentation and Testing (25 points): Comprehensive code comments explaining logic, clear user instructions, demonstration of testing different scenarios, and professional README file with usage examples

title: Advanced Calculus Applications: Multi-Variable Optimization in Real-World Contexts
description: Students will engage in structured discussions analyzing complex multi-variable optimization problems from engineering, economics, and physics, demonstrating mastery of partial derivatives, Lagrange multipliers, and constraint optimization while evaluating peer solutions and justifying mathematical approaches.
learning_objectives: Apply partial derivatives and gradient vectors to solve multi-variable optimization problems
Implement Lagrange multipliers method for constrained optimization scenarios
Analyze and critique mathematical solutions using precise mathematical language
Synthesize optimization techniques to model and solve real-world problems
criteria: Mathematical Accuracy and Methodology (25 points): Correct application of partial derivatives, Lagrange multipliers, and optimization techniques with proper mathematical notation and step-by-step reasoning
Problem Analysis and Interpretation (25 points): Clear identification of variables, constraints, and objective functions; accurate translation of real-world scenarios into mathematical models

Critical Evaluation and Peer Response (25 points): Thoughtful analysis of at least two peer solutions, identification of errors or alternative approaches, constructive feedback with mathematical justification
Communication and Mathematical Discourse (25 points): Clear, precise mathematical writing using appropriate terminology, logical flow of arguments, and professional discussion forum etiquette

title: Advanced Distributed Systems Architecture: Design and Defense Presentation
description: Students design and present a comprehensive distributed system architecture for a real-world scenario, demonstrating mastery of scalability patterns, fault tolerance mechanisms, consistency models, and performance optimization. The presentation includes a technical deep-dive, architectural justification, and defense against expert-level questioning.
learning_objectives: Design scalable distributed system architectures using appropriate patterns and technologies
Analyze and justify trade-offs between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance
Implement fault tolerance and disaster recovery strategies in distributed environments
Evaluate and optimize distributed system performance under various load conditions
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to expert audiences
criteria: System Design and Architecture (25 points): Demonstrates sophisticated understanding of distributed systems patterns, appropriate technology selection, clear component interaction diagrams, and scalability considerations with quantified metrics

Technical Depth and Accuracy (25 points): Shows expert-level knowledge of consensus algorithms, consistency models, fault tolerance mechanisms, and performance optimization techniques with accurate technical details and proper terminology

Critical Analysis and Trade-offs (25 points): Provides thorough analysis of CAP theorem implications, justified architectural decisions, comprehensive risk assessment, and alternative approach comparisons with quantified impact analysis

Presentation Quality and Defense (25 points): Delivers clear, professional presentation with effective visual aids, demonstrates mastery through confident responses to technical questions, and shows ability to think critically under pressure

title: Beginner Data Science Portfolio: Customer Sales Analysis Project
description: Students will create a complete data science portfolio demonstrating fundamental skills by analyzing a customer sales dataset. The portfolio includes data exploration, cleaning, visualization, basic statistical analysis, and insights presentation using Python and Jupyter notebooks.
learning_objectives: Apply data cleaning and preprocessing techniques to prepare raw data for analysis
Create meaningful visualizations to explore and communicate data insights
Perform basic statistical analysis and interpret results
Document data science workflow with clear explanations and conclusions
Use Python libraries (pandas, matplotlib, seaborn) for data manipulation and visualization
criteria: Data Exploration & Cleaning (25 points): Properly identifies missing values, duplicates, and data quality issues. Implements appropriate cleaning strategies. Documents cleaning decisions with clear rationale.

Data Visualization (25 points): Creates 5+ meaningful charts (histogram, scatter plot, bar chart, box plot, correlation matrix). Charts are properly labeled with titles, axes labels, and legends. Visualizations effectively communicate insights.

Statistical Analysis (25 points): Calculates relevant descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, standard deviation). Identifies patterns and trends in the data. Performs basic correlation analysis. Interprets results correctly.

Documentation & Presentation (25 points): Code is well-commented and organized. Provides clear markdown explanations between code cells. Includes executive summary with 3-5 key findings. Professional presentation with proper grammar and formatting.

title: Linear Regression Analysis Lab Report
description: Students will collect real-world data, perform linear regression analysis, and write a comprehensive lab report documenting their methodology, calculations, statistical analysis, and conclusions about the relationship between two variables.
learning_objectives: Apply linear regression techniques to analyze real-world data relationships
Calculate and interpret correlation coefficients and regression equations
Evaluate the validity and limitations of statistical models
Communicate mathematical findings through clear written analysis
criteria: Data Collection & Organization (25 points): Appropriate variable selection, minimum 20 data points, properly formatted tables, clear data source documentation
Mathematical Analysis (25 points): Correct calculation of correlation coefficient, accurate regression equation derivation, proper use of formulas and statistical methods
Statistical Interpretation (25 points): Meaningful analysis of R² value, discussion of correlation strength, identification of outliers, assessment of model limitations
Report Quality & Communication (25 points): Clear methodology explanation, logical organization, proper mathematical notation, evidence-based conclusions, professional presentation

title: Advanced Data Structures and Algorithm Complexity Analysis Quiz
description: Comprehensive assessment evaluating students' mastery of advanced data structures (B-trees, heaps, hash tables), algorithm design patterns, and asymptotic complexity analysis through theoretical problems and practical implementation scenarios.
learning_objectives: Analyze and compare time/space complexity of advanced data structures and algorithms using Big-O, Theta, and Omega notation
Design optimal algorithms for complex problems using appropriate data structures and algorithmic paradigms
Evaluate trade-offs between different data structure implementations in real-world scenarios
Apply mathematical reasoning to prove algorithm correctness and analyze worst-case, best-case, and average-case performance
criteria: Complexity Analysis (25 points): Correctly determines and justifies time/space complexity using formal notation, shows all mathematical work, identifies dominant terms, and explains reasoning clearly

Algorithm Design (25 points): Creates efficient, correct algorithms that solve given problems optimally, demonstrates understanding of algorithmic paradigms (divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy), and shows clear logical flow
Data Structure Application (25 points): Selects appropriate data structures for specific use cases, explains implementation details and operations, compares alternatives with valid justifications

Problem-Solving and Communication (25 points): Demonstrates systematic problem-solving approach, provides clear explanations with proper terminology, shows complete work with logical progression, and addresses all parts of multi-step problems

title: End-to-End Predictive Analytics Pipeline: Customer Churn Prediction System
description: Students will design, implement, and deploy a complete machine learning pipeline to predict customer churn using real-world telecommunications data. This capstone project assesses advanced data science competencies including feature engineering, model selection, performance optimization, and business interpretation.
learning_objectives: Apply advanced feature engineering techniques to transform raw business data into predictive features
Implement and compare multiple machine learning algorithms for binary classification problems
Optimize model performance using hyperparameter tuning and ensemble methods
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics for imbalanced datasets
Communicate technical findings to business stakeholders through clear visualizations and recommendations
Deploy machine learning models using cloud platforms or containerization technologies
criteria: Data Exploration & Feature Engineering (25 points): Comprehensive EDA with statistical insights, creative feature engineering including domain-specific variables, proper handling of missing data and outliers, feature selection using statistical methods

Model Development & Optimization (25 points): Implementation of at least 3 different algorithms (e.g., logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting), proper cross-validation strategy, hyperparameter optimization using grid/random search, ensemble methods or stacking techniques

Model Evaluation & Interpretation (25 points): Appropriate metrics for imbalanced data (precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC, AUC-PR), statistical significance testing, feature importance analysis, model interpretability using SHAP or LIME, business impact quantification

Technical Implementation & Deployment (25 points): Clean, well-documented code following best practices, reproducible pipeline with version control, model deployment (API endpoint, Docker container, or cloud service), comprehensive technical documentation and testing

title: Fundamentals of Arithmetic Operations and Problem Solving Exam
description: A comprehensive beginner-level mathematics exam covering basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), fractions, decimals, and real-world problem solving. Students will demonstrate computational skills and mathematical reasoning through various question formats including multiple choice, short answer, and word problems.
learning_objectives: Perform accurate calculations using the four basic arithmetic operations with whole numbers, fractions, and decimals
Apply mathematical reasoning to solve real-world word problems involving money, measurement, and time
Demonstrate understanding of place value, number relationships, and basic mathematical concepts
Show organized work and clear mathematical communication in problem-solving processes
criteria: Computational Accuracy (25 points): Correct execution of arithmetic operations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division with whole numbers, fractions, and decimals. Full credit for 90-100% accuracy, partial credit for 70-89%, minimal credit for 50-69%, no credit below 50%

Problem-Solving Strategy (25 points): Demonstrates logical approach to word problems, identifies relevant information, selects appropriate operations, and shows systematic work. Evaluates quality of mathematical reasoning and strategy selection rather than just final answers

Mathematical Communication (25 points): Shows clear, organized work with proper notation, labels units appropriately, explains reasoning where requested, and presents solutions in understandable format. Assesses clarity of mathematical expression and completeness of explanations

Application and Reasoning (25 points): Successfully interprets real-world contexts, makes connections between mathematical concepts, checks reasonableness of answers, and applies learned concepts to unfamiliar situations. Measures depth of understanding beyond memorized procedures

title: Algorithm Efficiency Analysis and Trade-off Discussion
description: Students will analyze and compare different algorithmic approaches to a common problem, evaluating time/space complexity trade-offs and discussing real-world implementation considerations through structured peer discussion and written analysis.
learning_objectives: Analyze time and space complexity of algorithms using Big O notation
Compare and contrast different algorithmic approaches to solve the same problem
Evaluate trade-offs between algorithm efficiency and implementation complexity
Communicate technical concepts clearly in both written and verbal formats
criteria: Complexity Analysis (25 points): Correctly identifies and explains time/space complexity using Big O notation, shows mathematical reasoning, identifies best/average/worst case scenarios

Algorithm Comparison (25 points): Provides thorough comparison of at least 3 different approaches, identifies strengths and weaknesses of each method, demonstrates understanding of when each approach is most suitable

Real-world Application (25 points): Discusses practical implementation considerations, addresses scalability concerns, considers memory constraints and hardware limitations, provides concrete examples of usage scenarios

Communication and Discussion Participation (25 points): Presents ideas clearly and logically, actively engages in peer discussion, asks thoughtful questions, provides constructive feedback to classmates, uses appropriate technical terminology

title: End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline: Business Impact Analysis and Presentation
description: Students will design, implement, and present a complete machine learning solution for a real-world business problem, demonstrating technical proficiency, business acumen, and communication skills through a comprehensive presentation to stakeholders.
learning_objectives: Apply advanced machine learning techniques to solve complex, real-world business problems
Demonstrate proficiency in data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, and hyperparameter optimization
Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics and statistical validation techniques
Communicate technical findings effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Assess business impact and provide actionable recommendations based on data science insights
Implement MLOps practices including model deployment, monitoring, and maintenance strategies
criteria: Technical Implementation (25 points): Demonstrates advanced ML techniques, proper data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection with justification, hyperparameter tuning, and code quality. Includes appropriate statistical validation and handles edge cases effectively.
